title: Runtime-model binding lifecycle and LTS routing broker
creator: Priya Desai
description: Design and implement a lifecycle model that binds model versions to compatible runtime versions via an explicit 'binding' object, supports LTS channels, and exposes deterministic routing and graceful fallback behavior when mismatches occur. This ticket covers the server-side routing broker, the runtime states and state machine for graceful fallback/rollback, API flags for pinning and opt-in upgrades, and the admin console controls and telemetry to operate safe rollouts.
background: We currently allow model-serving requests to be routed to the latest compatible runtime variant based on a compatibility matrix. As we expand LTS channels and more frequent runtime/optimizer changes, teams need precise controls for pinning (customer/route-level), a formal binding lifecycle to avoid silent incompatibilities, and robust fallback semantics for cross-version failures. Recent incidents showed surfaced errors when a model upgrade landed on a runtime with a subtle KV-cache KV layout change. We need machine-readable bindings, rollout gates, and observable rollback behaviors to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A new binding resource exists that maps: model_id + model_version -> runtime_version / runtime_channel (strings). 2) Router honors binding precedence: explicit binding > route pin > tenant default > floating compatibility. 3) LTS channels (e.g., stable-2026-01) can be targeted in bindings. 4) If a target runtime is unavailable or fails negotiation, router transitions to well-defined fallback states with exponential backoff and emits SLO/alert events. 5) Admin console UI surfaces binding at route/tenant level and allows staged rollout (canary %, ramp). 6) System tests validate cross-version traffic using synthetic prompts and verify KV-cache integrity across transitions. 7) Telemetry: per-request annotated headers show binding decision and fallback reason; dashboards show failure-rate delta and rollback counts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design): finalize binding schema and precedence rules; draft state machine for router and runtime negotiation. Phase 2 (server): implement binding CRUD and router selection logic; add fallback state machine handlers. Phase 3 (runtime): add negotiation hook that reports capability vector and accepts explicit runtime_version pin. Phase 4 (console/CLI): expose binding editor and staged rollout controls; add safety gates. Phase 5 (tests/telemetry): integration tests, e2e chaos tests simulating runtime failures, and dashboards/alerts. Phase 6 (gradual rollout): perform internal canary -> opt-in customers -> platform-wide rollout.
rollout_plan: - Canary (internal): 5% traffic to new binding broker with manual monitoring for 48h. - External opt-in: enable for customers who opt into early bindings (via admin toggle) for 1 week. - Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automated rollback if error-rate or latency regresses beyond thresholds. - Emergency rollback: binding broker must support immediate global failover to 'floating-compatible' routing when manual abort triggered. All stages require green health checks and SRE sign-off.
qa_test_plan: - Unit tests for binding precedence and CRUD. - Integration tests verifying router routes to pinned runtime and fallback path when runtime unregistered. - Chaos tests: kill runtime processes and verify backoff and rollback. - Compatibility test harness: run a matrix of model versions against runtime versions with regression prompts. - Load test at target QPS levels to ensure broker scales.
metrics_and_alerts: Create dashboards and alerts: 1) binding_decision_rate by reason, 2) binding_fallback_count, 3) binding_fallback_latency_p50/p95, 4) per-route error-rate delta post-binding-change, 5) rollback_trigger_count. Alert if fallback_count > 0.5% of requests for >30m or per-route error-rate increases by >2x.

progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with routing, runtime, and console leads. Agreed on binding precedence rules and LTS channel naming convention.
2026-03-04: PoC binding schema committed to design doc. Router selection algorithm draft posted.
2026-03-08: Runtime negotiation hook prototype implemented; added compatibility vector reporting. Initial integration tests green locally.
2026-03-10: Began server-side binding CRUD implementation; opened ENG-51603 for console UI work.
risks: - Incorrect precedence implementation could cause silent misrouting leading to model behavior drift. - Runtime capability vector may be incomplete, causing false incompatibility. - Telemetry gaps could make it hard to detect regressions quickly. - Rollout rollback automation must be bulletproof; mistakes would affect production traffic.
notes: Operational suggestions: add a 'binding-dry-run' mode that logs decisions without changing routing to validate for 24h. Consider adding a signing token for binding updates so that tenant-managed automation can audit changes. We should also make bindings immutable for a short TTL after creation to avoid thrash during rollouts.
